changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For retail buyers, especially the store operations or COO owner: "One system for the tills and the website." One customer, one basket, and one party accountable, so you don't have two vendors pointing at each other. Show it as a step-by-step return of an online order at the till, rather than claiming the line has disappeared. Use "the tills" in retail copy, not "unified commerce" or "point of sale."
changes.why: M3 got silence and was called "that's a diagram" by the store operations head, who then asked how a return works step by step, while the customer's own phrases were one system for tills and web, one customer one basket, and no two vendors pointing at each other.

changes.change: Add a retail proof pack for the pitch: a retailer the buyer can call, a sample rollout plan with dates, who installs, and what happens to the old tills, and a recorded live return at the till. Name the people on our side who will run the store rollout and the single owner accountable.
changes.why: The customer asked for a retailer they could call and a dated rollout plan and we sent a case study and described it, while Adyen reportedly came with a retail team, store-rollout experience and one contract, and our answer to who does installs was a partner.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For retail buyers: offer a named retailer they can speak to directly, matched to their kind of store estate, instead of pointing to customer stories generally.
changes.why: A case study did not satisfy a buyer who asked "can I talk to them?", and Adyen reportedly named retailers Angela knew.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For retail deals, open with the operational failure rather than the generic growth line: buy online, return in store, and the store can't see the online order because store and web are two different customer records. Aim it at the COO and store operations, not only the technical RFP contact.
changes.why: The trigger was a holiday returns failure from split customer records, which is a store operations problem, yet the evaluation ran through the CTO while Angela signed with Adyen.
